title: Hilary Swank Defends Motherhood at 47, Addresses Age Backlash
text:
Hilary Swank, who had twins at 47 in 2023, says she became a mother at the right time and addresses backlash over older motherhood. She opens up about criticism and parenting.
Hilary Swank, the 52-year-old Oscar-winning actress, has publicly addressed the backlash she faced for becoming a mother at 47. In a November 2025 profile with Women's Health, Swank revealed that she gave birth to twins Aya and Ohm in 2023, and she believes it was the right time in her life. She told the magazine that she would have had kids earlier but did not actively wait until 47. The interview highlights her journey into motherhood later in life and her response to critics.
Hilary Swank Discusses Motherhood Timing
Swank explained that becoming a parent at 47 was a magical culmination of her life. She said, "It was the right time for a myriad of reasons." The actress also noted that she froze her eggs at 37, which allowed her to have children later. She believes she is a different parent now than she would have been in her early 40s, citing increased patience and understanding. Swank emphasized that she is deeply interested in her children's brains and development.
She shared these insights in a November 2025 profile with Women's Health, where she opened up about her parenting philosophy. Swank's comments come as she continues to advocate for women who choose to have children later in life. She has been married to Philip Schneider, and the couple welcomed twins Aya and Ohm in 2023 when Swank was 48.
Backlash and Personal Stories
In a sneak peek of an episode slated to air on Tuesday, October 20, Swank discussed the backlash women face for having children older. She said, "There's a lot of backlash women get for having children older but not men, which is interesting." Swank also recalled a particularly intense reaction from a stranger. The woman said, "How dare you. You're too old and you won't be old enough when your kids are older and my dad was my favorite person and he died when I was in my 20s, my early 20s and it's just devastation." Swank shared this story, noting that she related to it because her own father had passed away and was one of her favorite people.
She explained that she would rather be born and have that favorite person and experience that than not at all. Swank's perspective highlights her resilience in the face of criticism. The episode is set to air on Tuesday, October 20, and Swank announced the sneak peek on Wednesday, October 14.
Family and Career
Swank and her husband Philip Schneider are officially the proud parents of twins. The Alaska Daily star shared the first photo of her newborns on Sunday, April 9, 2023, with the caption: "It wasn't easy. But boy (and girl!) was it worth it. Happy Easter!" She also posted that she was posting from pure Heaven. Swank's journey to motherhood was not easy, but she has embraced it fully.
Despite the backlash, Swank remains focused on her family and her career. She continues to act and has been open about her experiences. Her story resonates with many women who choose to have children later in life, and she hopes to inspire others. Swank's message is clear: motherhood at any age is a personal choice and can be a beautiful experience.
Support from Friends
Swank's friend and fellow actress, 51-year-old Charlize Theron, responded to her story with empathy. Theron said, "Oh my God, I mean it is weird, men have babies in their like 80s and that's not a euphemism or a joke. You had kids in your 40s and people weren't always gracious about it." Theron's support underscores the double standards women face regarding age and parenting.
Swank's openness about her experience has sparked conversations about older motherhood and the societal pressures women encounter. She continues to share her journey, hoping to empower others. With her twins Aya and Ohm, Swank is enjoying every moment of motherhood, proving that age is just a number when it comes to love and family.
